overview: This Senate resolution names August 1, 2026, as "Gold Star Children's Day." "Gold Star" families are those who have lost a loved one who died while serving in the U.S. armed forces, a tradition dating to World War I when families hung a flag with a gold star in their windows. The resolution honors the sacrifices and hardships of children whose parents died in military service and encourages Americans to observe the day in their support. The Senate has passed a similar resolution each year since 2021, and agreed to this one by unanimous consent on July 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say the children of fallen service members carry a lasting burden and deserve national recognition alongside the parents and spouses already honored.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, including benefits for military families.
